Let's dive into Chapter Six: Making Change Stick—Turning New Behaviors Into Lasting Habits.
So, you’ve got the six sources of influence working for you. That’s a huge win. But here’s where a lot of folks stumble—how do you keep that momentum going, so your new behaviors don’t just fizzle out after a few weeks?
Think about it: how many times have you started strong with a new routine, only to slip back into old habits before you know it? It’s normal, but it doesn’t have to be your story.
The real secret? Turning deliberate actions into automatic habits. Imagine building a path through a grassy field. At first, every step takes effort. But if you keep walking the same route, the grass flattens and the path gets clearer. Eventually, it’s the easiest way forward.
So, how do you make those new behaviors stick? Here are a few practical techniques you can use:
First, anchor your new habit to something you already do. Let’s say you want to drink more water—try making it part of your morning coffee routine. The coffee becomes a cue that reminds you to reach for that glass of water.
Next, start small. Really small. If you want to exercise more, begin with just five minutes a day—something that feels almost too easy to skip. Those quick wins add up, and before you know it, you’re building momentum.
And don’t underestimate the power of tracking your progress. A simple calendar, journal, or even an app can help you mark each day you stick with your new habit. Watching that streak grow? It’s surprisingly motivating.
But even with all that, you’ll probably hit a plateau. That’s the point where the initial excitement fades and things start to feel a bit stale. Don’t worry—this is totally normal. When that happens, go back to those six sources of influence. Maybe you need a new reward, a fresh social ally, or a tweak to your environment to keep things interesting.
Let me give you a real-world example. Imagine someone who wants to meditate every day. They might pair meditation with their morning coffee, start with just two minutes, and mark each session on a wall calendar. Over time, sitting quietly becomes as automatic as pouring that first cup.
So, here’s the key takeaway: lasting change isn’t about having endless willpower or perfect intentions. It’s about designing habits that fit naturally into your life—using cues, repetition, and small wins to make new behaviors your default choice.
